analysis.title: What's next for commodities?
key_insights: UBS CIO favors broad commodity exposure with active management. Leadership is expected to rotate as geopolitical conditions, inventories and demand expectations change.

Energy prices surged again on Middle East supply concerns. Dutch TTF gas hit a record EUR 104/MWh on 30 October. Brent rallied to USD 118/bbl last Friday, then fell to about USD 109/bbl early Monday on more dovish peace-talk headlines.
Middle East hostilities continue. Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have escalated in recent weeks, and attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz still pose supply risks.
Industrial metals such as copper are supported by AI infrastructure and electrification investment.
A strengthening El Niño is disrupting rainfall across major growing regions. This raises the potential effect of weather-related supply disruptions on agricultural prices.
Gold is expected to stay supported by central bank demand and reserve diversification, despite a more challenging near-term outlook. UBS calls it a useful strategic diversifier.
Commodities have shown low correlations with equities and bonds. From January 1999 through May 2026 the correlation was 0.44 with global equities and -0.04 with US bonds.
UBS suggests investors with large gold allocations and significant unrealized gains could add copper, aluminum and agricultural exposure to diversify future returns.

A diversified, regularly rebalanced exposure captures most of the asset class's benefits. Selective tilts can add value when conviction is high. Risks include price swings and costs of futures or physical holdings.

sector_views.rationale: Diversification, inflation resilience and structural demand trends amid supply-demand imbalances, geopolitical risks and the energy transition. Active management preferred.
AI infrastructure and electrification investment support copper and aluminum.
El Niño-related rainfall disruption raises weather-related supply risk.
Central bank demand and reserve diversification support it, but the near-term outlook is more challenging.

tension_points.bull_case: AI infrastructure and electrification support industrial metals, El Niño raises agricultural supply risk, and central bank demand supports gold. Commodities add diversification and inflation resilience.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy prices swing sharply on peace-talk headlines, gold faces a more challenging near-term outlook, and futures or physical holdings carry costs and price swings.
